newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria bank deal seen creating large synergies.
newsitem.headline: Austria bank deal seen creating large synergies.

text.p: The merger of Austria's two top banks, Bank Austria and Creditanstalt, will result in synergies of at least five billiion schillings a year, Bank Austria chief executive Gerhard Randa was quoted as saying.

In an interview with current affairs magazine Profil to be published on Monday, Randa said extra revenues for the combined bank were estimated "at five billion schillings annually under the most conservative assumptions".

Bank Austria in January bought the Austrian state's 70 percent voting stake in rival Creditanstalt, former banker to the Habsburg family of Austro-Hungarian emperors, for 17.2 billion schillings in cash. The merger will create the country's biggest bank with some 1,300 billion schillings in total assets.

The European Commission has yet to give its final approval to Austria's biggest corporate merger since World War Two. A statement by the commission is expected next week. ($ = 12.06 Austrian Schillings)
